units.leftText: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,
units.rightText: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—

units.leftText: which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,
units.rightText: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,

units.leftText: concerning his Son, who was born of the offspring of David according to the flesh,
units.rightText: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,

units.leftText: who was declared to be the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
units.rightText: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.leftText: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations for his name’s sake;
units.rightText: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

units.leftText: among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ;
units.rightText: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints:

units.leftText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
units.rightText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

units.leftText: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,
units.rightText: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

units.leftText: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.
units.rightText: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

units.leftText: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;
units.rightText: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,

units.leftText: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.
units.rightText: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

units.leftText: Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far), that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.
units.rightText: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

units.leftText: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
units.rightText: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

units.leftText: So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.
units.rightText: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

units.leftText: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
units.rightText: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.

units.leftText: For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”
units.rightText: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
rightNotes: 1:17 Literally For in it is revealed the righteousness of God from faith to faith

units.leftText: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
units.rightText: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

units.leftText: because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them.
units.rightText: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

units.leftText: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.
units.rightText: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.

units.leftText: Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.
units.rightText: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

units.leftText: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
units.rightText: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,

units.leftText: and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.
units.rightText: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

units.leftText: Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves;
units.rightText: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

units.leftText: who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
units.rightText: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

units.leftText: For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.
units.rightText: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

units.leftText: Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.
units.rightText: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

units.leftText: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;
units.rightText: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

units.leftText: being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers,
units.rightText: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,

units.leftText: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
units.rightText: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

units.leftText: without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful;
units.rightText: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

units.leftText: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.
units.rightText: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

units.leftText: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things.
units.rightText: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.

units.leftText: We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.
units.rightText: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.

units.leftText: Do you think this, O man who judges those who practice such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgment of God?
units.rightText: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?

units.leftText: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
units.rightText: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?

units.leftText: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgment of God,
units.rightText: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.

units.leftText: who “will pay back to everyone according to their works:”
units.rightText: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”

units.leftText: to those who by perseverance in well-doing seek for glory, honor, and incorruptibility, eternal life;
units.rightText: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.

units.leftText: but to those who are self-seeking and don’t obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, will be wrath, indignation,
units.rightText: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.

units.leftText: oppression, and anguish on every soul of man who does evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
units.rightText: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;

units.leftText: But glory, honor, and peace go to every man who does good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
units.rightText: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.

units.leftText: For there is no partiality with God.
units.rightText: For God does not show favoritism.

units.leftText: For as many as have sinned without the law will also perish without the law. As many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.
units.rightText: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.

units.leftText: For it isn’t the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified
units.rightText: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.

units.leftText: (for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves,
units.rightText: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.

units.leftText: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)
units.rightText: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them

units.leftText: in the day when God will judge the secrets of men, according to my Good News, by Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.

units.leftText: Indeed you bear the name of a Jew, rest on the law, glory in God,
units.rightText: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;

units.leftText: know his will, and approve the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,
units.rightText: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;

units.leftText: and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,
units.rightText: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,

units.leftText: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babies, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth.
units.rightText: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth —

units.leftText: You therefore who teach another, don’t you teach yourself? You who preach that a man shouldn’t steal, do you steal?
units.rightText: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

units.leftText: You who say a man shouldn’t commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
units.rightText: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

units.leftText: You who glory in the law, do you dishonor God by disobeying the law?
units.rightText: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?

units.leftText: For “the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you,” just as it is written.
units.rightText: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”

units.leftText: For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
units.rightText: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

units.leftText: If therefore the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, won’t his uncircumcision be accounted as circumcision?
units.rightText: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?

units.leftText: Won’t those who are physically uncircumcised, but fulfill the law, judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law?
units.rightText: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.

units.leftText: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;
units.rightText: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.

units.leftText: but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.
units.rightText: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.

units.leftText: Then what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the profit of circumcision?
units.rightText: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?

units.leftText: Much in every way! Because first of all, they were entrusted with the revelations of God.
units.rightText: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.

units.leftText: For what if some were without faith? Will their lack of faith nullify the faithfulness of God?
units.rightText: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?

units.leftText: May it never be! Yes, let God be found true, but every man a liar. As it is written,
units.rightText: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written:

units.leftText: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak like men do.
units.rightText: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.

units.leftText: May it never be! For then how will God judge the world?
units.rightText: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?

units.leftText: For if the truth of God through my lie abounded to his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
units.rightText: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?

units.leftText: Why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), “Let’s do evil, that good may come?” Those who say so are justly condemned.
units.rightText: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!

units.leftText: What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we previously warned both Jews and Greeks that they are all under sin.
units.rightText: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.

units.leftText: Now we know that whatever things the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may be brought under the judgment of God.
units.rightText: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.

units.leftText: Because by the works of the law, no flesh will be justified in his sight; for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
units.rightText: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.

units.leftText: But now apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified by the law and the prophets;
units.rightText: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.

units.leftText: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ to all and on all those who believe. For there is no distinction,
units.rightText: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,

units.leftText: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;
units.rightText: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

units.leftText: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: whom God sent to be an atoning sacrifice through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness through the passing over of prior sins, in God’s forbearance;
units.rightText: God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.

units.leftText: to demonstrate his righteousness at this present time, that he might himself be just and the justifier of him who has faith in Jesus.
units.rightText: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.

units.leftText: Where then is the boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith.
units.rightText: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.

units.leftText: We maintain therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.
units.rightText: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.

units.leftText: Or is God the God of Jews only? Isn’t he the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,
units.rightText: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,

units.leftText: since indeed there is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
units.rightText: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.

units.leftText: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! No, we establish the law.
units.rightText: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.

units.leftText: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh?
units.rightText: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has discovered?

units.leftText: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.
units.rightText: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

units.leftText: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”
units.rightText: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

units.leftText: Now to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace, but as something owed.
units.rightText: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

units.leftText: But to him who doesn’t work, but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is accounted for righteousness.
units.rightText: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.

units.leftText: Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:
units.rightText: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

units.rightText: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven,

units.rightText: Blessed is the man

units.leftText: Is this blessing then pronounced only on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say that faith was accounted to Abraham for righteousness.
units.rightText: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.

units.leftText: How then was it counted? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
units.rightText: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
rightNotes: 4:10 Literally How then was it reckoned—being in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

units.leftText: He received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision, that he might be the father of all those who believe, though they might be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might also be accounted to them.
units.rightText: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

units.leftText: He is the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had in uncircumcision.
units.rightText: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

units.leftText: For the promise to Abraham and to his offspring that he would be heir of the world wasn’t through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
units.rightText: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

units.leftText: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of no effect.
units.rightText: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,

units.leftText: For the law produces wrath; for where there is no law, neither is there disobedience.
units.rightText: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.

units.leftText: For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the offspring, not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.
units.rightText: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring — not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

units.leftText: As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were.
units.rightText: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.

units.leftText: Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.”
units.rightText: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

units.leftText: Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.
units.rightText: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

units.leftText: Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God,
units.rightText: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,

units.leftText: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.
units.rightText: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.

units.rightText: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited— for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

units.rightText: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.leftText: For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
units.rightText: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

units.leftText: For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a good person someone would even dare to die.
units.rightText: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

units.leftText: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
units.rightText: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

units.leftText: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God’s wrath through him.
units.rightText: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!

units.leftText: For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.
units.rightText: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!

units.leftText: Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
units.rightText: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

units.leftText: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so death passed to all men because all sinned.
units.rightText: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.

units.leftText: For until the law, sin was in the world; but sin is not charged when there is no law.
units.rightText: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.

units.leftText: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those whose sins weren’t like Adam’s disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of him who was to come.
units.rightText: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.

units.leftText: But the free gift isn’t like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
units.rightText: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!

units.leftText: The gift is not as through one who sinned; for the judgment came by one to condemnation, but the free gift followed many trespasses to justification.
units.rightText: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.

units.leftText: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; so much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

units.leftText: So then as through one trespass, all men were condemned; even so through one act of righteousness, all men were justified to life.
units.rightText: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.

units.leftText: For as through the one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.
units.rightText: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

units.leftText: The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly,
units.rightText: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,

units.leftText: that as sin reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
units.rightText: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.leftText: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
units.rightText: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?

units.leftText: May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?
units.rightText: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?

units.leftText: Or don’t you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
units.rightText: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

units.leftText: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
units.rightText: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.

units.leftText: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;
units.rightText: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

units.leftText: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.
units.rightText: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

units.leftText: For he who has died has been freed from sin.
units.rightText: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

units.leftText: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,
units.rightText: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.

units.leftText: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over him!
units.rightText: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.

units.leftText: For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.
units.rightText: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

units.leftText: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.
units.rightText: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.

units.leftText: Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
units.rightText: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.

units.leftText: For sin will not have dominion over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
units.rightText: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.

units.leftText: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? May it never be!
units.rightText: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!

units.leftText: Don’t you know that when you present yourselves as servants and obey someone, you are the servants of whomever you obey, whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
units.rightText: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?

units.leftText: But thanks be to God that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were delivered.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.

units.leftText: Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.
units.rightText: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

units.leftText: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh; for as you presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness for sanctification.
units.rightText: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

units.leftText: For when you were servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.
units.rightText: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.

units.leftText: What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
units.rightText: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.

units.leftText: But now, being made free from sin and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification and the result of eternal life.
units.rightText: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.

units.leftText: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: Or don’t you know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?
units.rightText: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?
leftNotes: 7:1 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.
units.rightText: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.

units.leftText: So then if, while the husband lives, she is joined to another man, she would be called an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she is joined to another man.
units.rightText: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might produce fruit to God.
units.rightText: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

units.leftText: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law worked in our members to bring out fruit to death.
units.rightText: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.

units.leftText: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that in which we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.
units.rightText: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.

units.leftText: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn’t have known sin except through the law. For I wouldn’t have known coveting unless the law had said, “You shall not covet.”
units.rightText: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”

units.leftText: But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
units.rightText: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

units.leftText: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, sin revived and I died.
units.rightText: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.

units.leftText: The commandment which was for life, this I found to be for death;
units.rightText: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.

units.leftText: for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
units.rightText: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.

units.leftText: Therefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, righteous, and good.
units.rightText: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

units.leftText: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, was producing death in me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.
units.rightText: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.

units.leftText: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
units.rightText: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

units.leftText: For I don’t understand what I am doing. For I don’t practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.
units.rightText: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.

units.leftText: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, I consent to the law that it is good.
units.rightText: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.

units.leftText: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
units.rightText: In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

units.leftText: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwells no good thing. For desire is present with me, but I don’t find it doing that which is good.
units.rightText: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.

units.leftText: For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practice.
units.rightText: For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.

units.leftText: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
units.rightText: And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

units.leftText: I find then the law that, while I desire to do good, evil is present.
units.rightText: So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.

units.leftText: For I delight in God’s law after the inward person,
units.rightText: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.

units.leftText: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
units.rightText: But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.
rightNotes: 7:23 Literally captive to the law of sin being in my members.

units.leftText: What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?
units.rightText: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

units.leftText: I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord! So then with the mind, I myself serve God’s law, but with the flesh, sin’s law.
units.rightText: Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord!

units.leftText: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
units.rightText: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
leftNotes: 8:1 NU omits “who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit”
rightNotes: 8:1 BYZ and TR in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

units.leftText: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.
units.rightText: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.

units.leftText: For what the law couldn’t do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh,
units.rightText: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,
rightNotes: 8:3 Literally in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin

units.leftText: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
units.rightText: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

units.leftText: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
units.rightText: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

units.leftText: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
units.rightText: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,

units.leftText: because the mind of the flesh is hostile toward God, for it is not subject to God’s law, neither indeed can it be.
units.rightText: because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.

units.leftText: Those who are in the flesh can’t please God.
units.rightText: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
rightNotes: 8:8 Literally Those being in the flesh; similarly in verse 9

units.leftText: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
units.rightText: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.

units.leftText: If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
units.rightText: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
rightNotes: 8:10 Or yet the Spirit is life

units.leftText: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
units.rightText: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.
rightNotes: 8:11 NA, BYZ, and TR raised Christ from the dead

units.leftText: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.
units.rightText: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.

units.leftText: For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
units.rightText: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

units.leftText: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
units.rightText: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

units.leftText: For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
units.rightText: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
leftNotes: 8:15 Abba is an Aramaic word for “Father” or “Daddy”, which can be used affectionately and respectfully in prayer to our Father in heaven.

units.leftText: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
units.rightText: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.

units.leftText: and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
units.rightText: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ — if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.

units.leftText: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us.
units.rightText: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.

units.leftText: For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
units.rightText: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.

units.leftText: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope
units.rightText: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope

units.leftText: that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
units.rightText: that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.

units.leftText: For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.
units.rightText: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.

units.leftText: Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
units.rightText: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.

units.leftText: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?
units.rightText: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?

units.leftText: But if we hope for that which we don’t see, we wait for it with patience.
units.rightText: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.

units.leftText: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
units.rightText: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.

units.leftText: He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.
units.rightText: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

units.leftText: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
units.rightText: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.

units.leftText: For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
units.rightText: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
leftNotes: 8:29 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.
units.rightText: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.

units.leftText: What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
units.rightText: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

units.leftText: He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
units.rightText: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?

units.leftText: Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
units.rightText: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.

units.leftText: Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.
units.rightText: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God— and He is interceding for us.

units.leftText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
units.rightText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

units.leftText: Even as it is written,
units.rightText: As it is written:

units.leftText: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
units.rightText: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.

units.leftText: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
units.rightText: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,

units.leftText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit
units.rightText: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
units.rightText: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.

units.leftText: For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers’ sake, my relatives according to the flesh
units.rightText: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,

units.leftText: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises;
units.rightText: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.

units.leftText: of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God, blessed forever. Amen.
units.rightText: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.

units.leftText: But it is not as though the word of God has come to nothing. For they are not all Israel that are of Israel.
units.rightText: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.

units.leftText: Neither, because they are Abraham’s offspring, are they all children. But, “your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac.”
units.rightText: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”

units.leftText: That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as heirs.
units.rightText: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.

units.leftText: For this is a word of promise: “At the appointed time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”
units.rightText: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”

units.leftText: Not only so, but Rebekah also conceived by one, by our father Isaac.
units.rightText: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.

units.leftText: For being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him who calls,
units.rightText: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
leftNotes: 9:11 NU puts the phrase “not of works, but of him who calls” at the beginning of verse 12 instead of the end of verse 11.

units.leftText: it was said to her, “The elder will serve the younger.”
units.rightText: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”

units.rightText: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

units.leftText: I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean of itself; except that to him who considers anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
units.rightText: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

units.leftText: Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Don’t destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
units.rightText: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

units.leftText: Then don’t let your good be slandered,
units.rightText: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

units.leftText: for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: For he who serves Christ in these things is acceptable to God and approved by men.
units.rightText: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

units.leftText: So then, let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.
units.rightText: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

units.leftText: Don’t overthrow God’s work for food’s sake. All things indeed are clean, however it is evil for that man who creates a stumbling block by eating.
units.rightText: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

units.leftText: It is good to not eat meat, drink wine, nor do anything by which your brother stumbles, is offended, or is made weak.
units.rightText: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
rightNotes: 14:21 SBL, BYZ, and TR include or to be hindered or weakened.

units.leftText: Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is he who doesn’t judge himself in that which he approves.
units.rightText: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
rightNotes: 14:22 Literally Keep the faith that you have to yourself before God

units.leftText: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it isn’t of faith; and whatever is not of faith is sin.
units.rightText: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
rightNotes: 14:23 Some manuscripts place the text of Romans 16:25–27|ROM 16:25-27* here.

units.leftText: Now to him who is able to establish you according to my Good News and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret through long ages,
but now is revealed, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known for obedience of faith to all the nations;
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever! Amen.
leftNotes: 14:26 TR places verses 24-26 after Romans 16:24 as verses 25-27.

units.leftText: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
units.rightText: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

units.leftText: Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, to be building him up.
units.rightText: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.

units.leftText: For even Christ didn’t please himself. But, as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”
units.rightText: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”

units.leftText: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
units.rightText: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

units.leftText: Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
units.rightText: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

units.leftText: Now I say that Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers,
units.rightText: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,

units.leftText: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written,
units.rightText: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written:

units.leftText: Again he says,
units.rightText: Again, it says:

units.leftText: Again,
units.rightText: And again:

units.leftText: Again, Isaiah says,
units.rightText: And once more, Isaiah says:

units.leftText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.
units.rightText: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
leftNotes: 15:14 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: But I write the more boldly to you in part as reminding you, because of the grace that was given to me by God,
units.rightText: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me

units.leftText: that I should be a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the Good News of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I have therefore my boasting in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.
units.rightText: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.

units.leftText: For I will not dare to speak of any things except those which Christ worked through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,
units.rightText: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,

units.leftText: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of God’s Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Good News of Christ;
units.rightText: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
rightNotes: 15:19 SBL the power of the Spirit; NE and WH the power of the Holy Spirit

units.leftText: yes, making it my aim to preach the Good News, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build on another’s foundation.
units.rightText: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.

units.leftText: But, as it is written,
units.rightText: Rather, as it is written:

units.leftText: Therefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you,
units.rightText: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

units.leftText: but now, no longer having any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come to you,
units.rightText: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,

units.leftText: whenever I travel to Spain, I will come to you. For I hope to see you on my journey, and to be helped on my way there by you, if first I may enjoy your company for a while.
units.rightText: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.

units.leftText: But now, I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
units.rightText: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

units.leftText: For it has been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints who are at Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Yes, it has been their good pleasure, and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to serve them in material things.
units.rightText: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

units.leftText: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by way of you to Spain.
units.rightText: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.

units.leftText: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of the Good News of Christ.
units.rightText: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
rightNotes: 15:29 TR and BYZ include of the gospel.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,
units.rightText: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.

units.leftText: that I may be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
units.rightText: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,

units.leftText: that I may come to you in joy through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.
units.rightText: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.

units.leftText: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
units.rightText: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
rightNotes: 15:33 Some manuscripts do not include Amen.One early manuscript places the text of Romans 16:25–27|ROM 16:25-27* here.

units.leftText: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,
units.rightText: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

units.leftText: that you receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.
units.rightText: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

units.leftText: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
rightNotes: 16:3 Prisca is a variant of Priscilla; see Acts 18:2|ACT 18:2*.

units.leftText: who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the Gentiles.
units.rightText: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.

units.leftText: Greet the assembly that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Achaia to Christ.
units.rightText: Greet also the church that meets at their house.

units.leftText: Greet Mary, who labored much for us.
units.rightText: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.

units.leftText: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
units.rightText: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.

units.leftText: Greet Amplias, my beloved in the Lord.
units.rightText: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
units.rightText: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.

units.leftText: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.
units.rightText: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ.

units.leftText: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
units.rightText: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman.

units.leftText: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
units.rightText: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
units.rightText: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.

units.leftText: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
units.rightText: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
leftNotes: 16:14 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
units.rightText: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

units.leftText: Greet one another with a holy kiss. The assemblies of Christ greet you.
units.rightText: Greet one another with a holy kiss.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers, look out for those who are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and turn away from them.
units.rightText: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.

units.leftText: For those who are such don’t serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
units.rightText: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.

units.leftText: For your obedience has become known to all. I rejoice therefore over you. But I desire to have you wise in that which is good, but innocent in that which is evil.
units.rightText: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

units.leftText: And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet.
units.rightText: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
rightNotes: 16:20 NA, NE, and WH Lord Jesus

units.leftText: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
units.rightText: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.

units.leftText: I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.
units.rightText: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.

units.leftText: Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.
units.rightText: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings.

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.

units.rightText: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past
leftNotes: 16:25 TR places Romans 14:24-26 at the end of Romans instead of at the end of chapter 14, and numbers these verses 16:25-27.

units.rightText: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith —
to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
rightNotes: 16:27 Some manuscripts place the text of verses 25–27 after Romans 14:23|ROM 14:23* or after Romans 15:33.
